Neil Young pulls his music from ALL streaming services claiming they have 'worst sound quality in history'

Getting real sick and tired of music snobs that think the majority of people can tell the difference between 192kbps and 256. Shit, 128kbps is still adequate for all but the most technical electronica. Not to mention, a lot of the higher-end phones and music players nowadays support FLAC and higher bit-rate lossy formats. I like Neil's music, but he's just trying to look "hipster cool" and push his own PonoPlayer garbage.

Fun fact: actively practicing musical composition and performance causes you to develop more precise and comprehensive hearing. The audience might not be able to tell the difference in quality, but to a career musician it's not about being "hipster cool." It just probably sounds like night and day to them.

Although yeah, his main goal here is obviously to push his PonoPlayer.

Can confirm: I have a small studio of mine in L.A and I can most assuredly tell the difference between 128kbp/s and 256 especially when I have my cans on but out of my monitors it is even worse. The biggest give away in lower quality music streams are the mids, they embellish those frequencies because that's where most vocals sit and most people listen to music for vocals. I can understand why he would be upset but in reality it seems more smart to just have your music across all platforms.

As an actively practicing composer and performer (though obviously not anywhere close to Neil Young's level), I definitely agree. It just bugs me when people come off as so superior because they look down on different technologies.

it's not only the kbps compression but also the 16bit compression that always killed it for me. the combination of both really does affect the overall feel of recording more than you know,

for someone who spends a lot of time recording, it must be irritating spending all that effort on a sound and having it destroyed by compression. 30 years, and digital music is still largely 16 bit.
